name: VIETNAM

flag.title: Cờ đỏ sao vàng
flag.note: Red field, one gold star since 1945

lead: Vietnam is a long, thin country shaped like the letter S. More than 100 million people live here. Their language has six musical tones. Rice terraces climb the northern hills. Limestone islands dot the southern sea.

geo: Vietnam is 1,650 km long but only 50 km wide at its narrowest. The Red River Delta and tall mountains fill the north. The Annamite Range runs south like a spine.
The Mekong Delta is a maze of rivers and floating markets. Vietnam has nearly 3,000 km of coast and over 3,000 islands. Hạ Long Bay is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
animals: The saola, the Asian unicorn, was found only in 1992. Almost nobody has photographed one alive. Indochinese tigers and clouded leopards prowl the border forests.
Dugongs graze on sea grass near Hạ Long Bay. Vietnam has nearly 1,000 bird species, more than all of Europe. The Vietnamese pheasant lives nowhere else.
culture: Vietnam has 54 ethnic groups. Tết, the Lunar New Year, is the biggest party. Dragon dancers fill the streets, and children get red envelopes of lucky money.
Phở broth simmers for hours with star anise and charred ginger. Bánh mì is a crusty baguette with Vietnamese fillings. Hội An glows with silk lanterns every night.
history: Đông Sơn people beat bronze drums 2,500 years ago. China ruled for 1,000 years. In 938 AD, Ngô Quyền beat a Chinese fleet with stakes hidden under the tide.
France took control in the 1800s. Hồ Chí Minh led the fight for independence. The country reunited in 1975. Today it is one of Asia's fastest-growing economies.
wows: Over 80% of the world's processed cashews come from Vietnam.
Around 1,969 limestone islands dot Hạ Long Bay, many hollow.
Tiny accent marks change a Vietnamese word's tone and meaning.
Hang Sơn Đoòng, the world's largest cave, has its own jungle.
The áo dài, Vietnam's national dress, is nearly 300 years old.
Vietnam is the second-largest coffee exporter, growing robusta in the highlands.
Water puppet shows, rối nước, are over 1,000 years old.

myths.myth: Everyone in Vietnam has a different family name
myths.fact: No. About 4 in 10 Vietnamese people share the family name Nguyễn.

myths.myth: Tết falls on the same day every year
myths.fact: No. Tết follows the moon, so it lands between late January and mid-February.
